Answer both questions beginning each answer on a new page in the answer booklet. Both answers carry equal marks.

Credit will be given for accuracy, correct use of a variety of expressions, verbs, vocabulary and idioms.

Use blue ink only.

incertitudes: Le sujet imprimé dit « Two Hours » : duree_epreuve vaut donc "2h" (la session 2023 avait "1h30"). Structure identique à 2023 : traduction (80 points) puis un essai à choisir parmi 3 sujets (80 points).

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Translate into French**

> Villagers like fishing a lot especially where there are rivers. When they catch fish, they eat some and sell the rest. The money they raise from their sales enables them to buy other needs such as soap, salt, pepper and palm oil.

> It was dry season and an ideal time for fishing. My elder brother took his net and his bag. He invited me to go with him to the nearby river. Unfortunately, I was not very well that day. I was suffering from headache. At about 6 o'clock in the morning, he left the house alone.

> He arrived there when no one had been to the river. He threw his net into the river. He was lucky that day. He caught much fish.

> On his way back, he met some customers. They bought some of the fish and he also brought a good quantity home.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Model translation**

Les villageois aiment beaucoup la pêche, surtout là où il y a des rivières. Quand ils attrapent du poisson, ils en mangent une partie et vendent le reste. L'argent qu'ils tirent de ces ventes leur permet d'acheter d'autres produits de première nécessité, comme le savon, le sel, le piment et l'huile de palme.

C'était la saison sèche et le moment idéal pour la pêche. Mon grand frère prit son filet et son sac. Il m'invita à l'accompagner à la rivière voisine. Malheureusement, je n'étais pas très bien ce jour-là. Je souffrais d'un mal de tête. Vers 6 heures du matin, il quitta la maison seul.

Il arriva là-bas alors que personne n'était encore allé à la rivière. Il jeta son filet dans l'eau. Il eut de la chance ce jour-là. Il attrapa beaucoup de poisson.

Sur le chemin du retour, il rencontra des clients. Ils achetèrent une partie du poisson et il rapporta aussi une bonne quantité à la maison.

**Translation points**

| Point | Trap | Correct form |
|---|---|---|
| General statements in the first paragraph | Using a past tense for what villagers do in general | Present tense: *aiment*, *attrapent*, *mangent*, *vendent*, *permet* |
| "eat some and sell the rest" | Leaving out the pronoun: *ils mangent quelques* | *ils en mangent une partie et vendent le reste* (the pronoun *en* replaces "some of the fish") |
| "The money they raise from their sales" | *l'argent qu'ils lèvent de leurs ventes* | *l'argent qu'ils tirent de ces ventes* (*tirer de* = to get from; relative pronoun *que*, direct object) |
| "needs such as soap, salt..." | *besoins tels que* (literal and awkward) | *produits de première nécessité, comme le savon, le sel...* (the article is repeated before each noun) |
| "It was dry season" | *Il était saison sèche* | *C'était la saison sèche* (*c'était* + noun, with the article) |
| "took", "invited", "left", "arrived", "threw", "caught", "met" | Mixing passé simple, passé composé and imparfait for a series of completed actions | Passé simple throughout (*prit, invita, quitta, arriva, jeta, eut, attrapa, rencontra*); the passé composé throughout is also accepted |
| "I was not very well", "I was suffering" | Using the passé simple for a state | Imparfait for a state or an ongoing situation: *je n'étais pas très bien*, *je souffrais* |
| "suffering from headache" | *souffrir de headache*, or *du mal de tête* with the wrong article | *souffrir d'un mal de tête* (or *avoir mal à la tête*) |
| "my elder brother" | *mon frère plus âgé* | *mon grand frère* (*mon frère aîné* is also correct) |
| "to go with him" | *aller avec lui* kept word for word | *l'accompagner* (more natural; *aller avec lui* is also accepted) |
| "At about 6 o'clock" | *à environ 6 o'clock* | *vers 6 heures* (or *vers six heures*) |
| "when no one had been to the river" | *quand personne a été*; no pluperfect | *alors que personne n'était encore allé à la rivière* (plus-que-parfait; *aller* takes *être*, so *allé*; negation *ne ... personne*) |
| "He caught much fish" | *beaucoup des poissons* | *beaucoup de poisson* ("fish" as a mass) or *beaucoup de poissons* |
| "brought a good quantity home" | *amener* (used for a person) | *rapporter* (a thing; *apporter* is also accepted); *à la maison* for "home" |

**Marking note**

The text is short, so every sentence counts. Credit goes to accuracy (tenses, agreements, accents) and to natural French rather than word-for-word translation.

**Common mistakes**

1. Leaving out a sentence or part of a sentence (for example "He was lucky that day" or "the nearby river"). Everything in the source must be translated.
2. Using one tense for the whole text. The general statements are in the present, the scene is described in the imparfait, and the events are in the passé simple or passé composé.
